statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let n = len(word). Then r is a duplicate-free list whose entries are exactly all valid generalized abbreviations of word, in any order. Formally: (1) for every byte vector s, there exists j with 0 <= j < len(r) and r[j] = s if and only if there exists a Boolean mask m on the indices 0,...,n-1 such that s is obtained by scanning i = 0,...,n-1, writing word[i] when m(i) is false, and writing the ASCII decimal representation of the length of each maximal consecutive run of true indices once at the start of that run; (2) for all j,k with 0 <= j < len(r) and 0 <= k < len(r), if r[j] = r[k] then j = k.
preconditions: word is a byte array with 1 <= len(word) <= 15, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(word), word[i] is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= word[i] <= 122).
